summary.headline: 20 of 30 random charts returned; 3 of 33 charts (9%) support a lower level than billed, under the rule threshold
summary.rationale: 1000000005 billed 99215 on 11.1% of 2,415 claims against an expected 5.5% given patient complexity (risk-adjusted score 4.62; plain z-score vs peers 1.19). 33% of this provider's 99215 claims were on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions. Records came back for 33 claims. Of 1 documented 99215 claims, 0 (0%) were documented below the billed level, against 33% for the comparison providers. Note checks on 20 returned notes (share showing each sign): problems 15%, late 25%, unsigned 0%, data 10%. No audit trail was received. 26 of 26 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed had no lab or test line on the claim. The 99215 share is 2.03 times expected over 2,415 claims. The office returned 20 of 30 random charts, and the follow-up got no response. Missing charts are not evidence of upcoding. No documented 99215 visits came back. Across the pooled charts, 3 of 33 (9%) support a lower level than billed, and the chart rule did not trigger. 25% of the notes were signed late, but the cloned-note rule applies only above 3 times expected, so it does not apply here. The rules leave this provider inconclusive, and no demand goes out. Examples: C0003352: billed 99214; documented MDM level low, 25 minutes. C0003854: billed 99213; documented MDM level straightforward, 5 minutes. C0002181: billed 99215, patient aged 51 with 1 chronic condition(s) (hyperlipidemia). C0002304: billed 99215, patient aged 50 with 0 chronic condition(s).
next_steps: 33 charts came back but do not settle it: request a targeted sample of 99215 charts, starting with C0003352, C0003854, C0002181.
Re-check after the targeted charts arrive; do not call upcoding or a sicker panel on this evidence alone.
